content.title: A look back at former Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax’s political career, personal struggles
content.text: RICHMOND, Va. (WWBT) - Justin Fairfax was sworn in as Virginia’s 41st lieutenant governor in January 2018 at 38 years old, becoming only the second African American ever elected to statewide office in the Commonwealth.“It’s a really powerful thing, in a lot of ways. I think it represents the progress we as Virginians have been able to make,” Fairfax said in a 2018 interview.He was considered a rising star in Virginia politics, until serious accusations derailed his path.Only a year into his term, Fairfax became embroiled in controversy when two women made sexual assault and rape allegations against him.Vanessa Tyson alleged Fairfax forced her to perform oral sex in a hotel room during the 2004 Democratic National Convention in Boston.Meredith Watson alleged that Fairfax raped her in 2000 while they were both undergraduates at Duke University.“Can’t fight back because you may not, you may lack, the kind of credibility that comes up so often in these, in the ‘Me Too Movement,’” said Tyson in an interview after she went public with her story.Fairfax maintained the interactions were consensual.“I did not lock the door, I did not turn out the lights, I did not hold her down or use any physical force whatsoever,” Fairfax said.He was never charged, but calls for his resignation poured in, including from members of his own Democratic Party.“I believe these women. He needs to resign immediately. These are very serious accusations and he’s unfit to serve office,” said Del. Patrick Hope, D-Arlington.Fairfax remained in office, often positioning himself as a supporter of stricter gun control measures. In March 2020, he broke a tie vote to pass a bill requiring gun owners report lost or stolen firearms to police within 48 hours.He announced plans to run for governor of Virginia in 2021. But Virginia voters failed to back him, with Fairfax losing in the Democratic primary.The former federal prosecutor left elected office in 2022. He reportedly bought a gun the same year.In the summer of 2024, his wife of nearly two decades, Dr. Cerina Fairfax, a dentist in Northern Virginia, petitioned to separate. She officially filed for divorce a year later.A judge overseeing the divorce noted in a legal order that Fairfax had spent the last few years cloistered in his home, struggling with alcohol abuse and mental health issues.Legal documents show Fairfax was ordered to vacate the shared home by the end of the month. Investigators believe could have been the tipping point that prompted him to kill his wife and then turn the gun on himself.Copyright 2026 WWBT. All rights reserved.
